content.title:
Scored quiz
Module 5
content.intro: This quiz covers all the lessons in this module. You must achieve 80% to pass. Good luck!

questions.prompt: What are the three key principles of effective energy governance discussed in the module?

correct.title: Correct
correct.body: Effectiveness, accountability, and inclusiveness ensure energy policies are sound, fair, and participatory.

wrong.title: Incorrect
wrong.body: Effectiveness, accountability, and inclusiveness ensure energy policies are sound, fair, and participatory.

questions.prompt: Which of the following best defines energy governance?

options.value: The enforcement of environmental regulations by government institutions
The management of climate financing mechanisms through public policy
The exercise of authority to manage the planning, production, and access to energy
The use of technology to reduce carbon emissions in energy systems

correct.title: Correct
correct.body: Energy governance involves political, economic, and social authority over energy decisions.

wrong.title: Incorrect
wrong.body: Energy governance involves political, economic, and social authority over energy decisions.

questions.prompt: Why is energy governance critical in achieving a just energy transition?

options.value: It ensures new technologies are patented fairly
It controls global emissions through a single regulatory agency
It shapes how decisions are made, trade-offs are managed, and policies are implemented
It focuses solely on reducing fossil fuel subsidies

correct.title: Correct
correct.body: Governance shapes policies and implementation, crucial for managing transition trade-offs.

wrong.title: Incorrect
wrong.body: Governance shapes policies and implementation, crucial for managing transition trade-offs.

questions.prompt: What does “fossil fuel lock-in” refer to?

options.value: Fossil fuels becoming inaccessible due to international sanctions
Political and economic dependence on fossil fuels, making transition difficult
Locking fossil fuels in underground reserves through carbon capture
Binding international contracts that prevent the use of renewables

correct.title: Correct
correct.body: Fossil fuel lock-in ties economies and institutions to fossil fuel dependence.

wrong.title: Incorrect
wrong.body: Fossil fuel lock-in ties economies and institutions to fossil fuel dependence.

questions.prompt: Which governance approach emphasizes collaboration across multiple levels and sectors?

correct.title: Correct
correct.body: Multi-level governance coordinates actions across levels and sectors.

wrong.title: Incorrect
wrong.body: Multi-level governance coordinates actions across levels and sectors.

questions.prompt: What tool is used to analyze how power and institutions shape policy outcomes in energy governance?

correct.title: Correct
correct.body: ICA identifies power dynamics and institutional barriers in policy processes.

wrong.title: Incorrect
wrong.body: ICA identifies power dynamics and institutional barriers in policy processes.

questions.prompt: According to the Paris Agreement, how are energy transitions now treated compared to earlier frameworks like the UNFCCC?

options.value: As side effects of agricultural transformation
As central policy levers essential for meeting climate goals
As voluntary measures with no legal standing
As actions to be undertaken solely by developed countries

correct.title: Correct
correct.body: The Paris Agreement centralizes energy transitions to meet climate goals.

wrong.title: Incorrect
wrong.body: The Paris Agreement centralizes energy transitions to meet climate goals.

questions.prompt: What percentage of Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) explicitly address just transition according to the synthesis report?

correct.title: Correct
correct.body: Only 31% of NDCs address just transition impacts on vulnerable groups.

wrong.title: Incorrect
wrong.body: Only 31% of NDCs address just transition impacts on vulnerable groups.

questions.prompt: Which foresight method starts by defining a desired future and then maps steps backward?

correct.title: Correct
correct.body: Backcasting is a foresight technique that begins with a desirable future and maps necessary steps to reach that vision.

wrong.title: Incorrect
wrong.body: Backcasting is a foresight technique that begins with a desirable future and maps necessary steps to reach that vision.

questions.prompt: What is the primary goal of a Whole-of-Government approach in energy governance?

options.value: To centralize power under the Ministry of Energy
To foster inter-ministerial collaboration and policy coherence
To reduce the role of parliament in energy governance

correct.title: Correct
correct.body: Whole-of-Government approaches integrate cross-ministerial collaboration to promote cohesive energy policy aligned with broader development goals.

wrong.title: Incorrect
wrong.body: Whole-of-Government approaches integrate cross-ministerial collaboration to promote cohesive energy policy aligned with broader development goals.

questions.prompt: Which of the following best defines agile oversight in the energy sector?

correct.title: Correct
correct.body: Agile oversight refers to real-time, adaptive monitoring that supports flexible decision-making and policy responsiveness in evolving contexts.

wrong.title: Incorrect
wrong.body: Agile oversight refers to real-time, adaptive monitoring that supports flexible decision-making and policy responsiveness in evolving contexts.

questions.prompt: Which of the following mechanisms are critical to external oversight in energy governance?

correct.title: Correct
correct.body: External oversight includes formal regulatory and legislative mechanisms as well as participatory approaches, all aimed at ensuring transparency and accountability.

wrong.title: Incorrect
wrong.body: External oversight includes formal regulatory and legislative mechanisms as well as participatory approaches, all aimed at ensuring transparency and accountability.
